issues.claim: T-V3-39 (c) runs before its provider lands. The clause covers restoration: 'a restoration from level 1 to 0 removes the damage in reverse threshold order …; a restoration with no Works removes it at once, every patch drawn; a roof bay the roofless state opened is patched once the wing is roofed; an element a restoring re-cut or a later `extend` adds is drawn as built … (V06 §3.23 (3))'. It runs on the damage fixtures' 'one restored with patches' (V03 l. 2849). Its timing cell (V03 l. 2906) runs every clause 'from P4', apart from (e)'s and (h)'s exports and the scrub, saying only 'before M6-E the levels at V11's default age'. V03 §8's P4 cell (l. 2943) runs 'T-V3-39 but (e) and (h)'s exports'. Restoration and the per-element peak come from V06 §3.23 (3), which V06's E2 builds (V06 §8 l. 4230: 'the decay level (item 123 (b), V06 §3.23: `decayLevel`, `decayPeak`, restoration …)'). Until E2 lands, V02's X36 (l. 4198) is the stand-in, reading 'the level from the existence state at V11's default age, nothing repaired'. §13.8's T123 row (l. 19491) likewise lands 'T123-4's epoch clause with M6-E'. Round 6 scheduled V02's twin clauses (T-V2-59's restoration in reverse threshold order, its patches and the manor's `extend`) 'at the later of M6b and V06's E2 … since until E2 lands V02 reads X36's stand-in — nothing repaired' (V02 §8.6 l. 3897–3904; R6-09). V03 reads the same V06 functions (V03 l. 196–197), but its clause stays at P4. M6-P's rest and M6-E run on separate tracks (INDEX l. 81–85, 103–105), so P4 may exit before E2, and at that point (c) cannot pass: a restored building reads level 0 and draws no patch. This is R6-09's class (VV12-r5-02, VV34-r5-01). Nothing built changes.
issues.required_change: T-V3-39's timing cell: "its scrub across the run at the later of P4 and V06's E6 (V06 §3.15.2's frames)" → "its scrub across the run at the later of P4 and V06's E6 (V06 §3.15.2's frames); (c) at the later of P4 and V06's E2 (V06 §3.23 (3)'s restorations and `decayPeak`, which E2 builds; until then nothing is repaired, V02 §8.6)". V03 §8's P4 tests cell: "T-V3-39 but (e) and (h)'s exports, its scrub across the run at the later of P4 and V06's E6" → "T-V3-39 but (e) and (h)'s exports, its scrub across the run at the later of P4 and V06's E6 and its (c) at the later of P4 and V06's E2".

issues.claim: The way-and-channel table's row (a) (base l. 2582) lists 'a stage-2 seed's way' among its subjects. Its ladder cell names 'V01 §3.17.3 (3)'s F-TEMPLATE rungs and §4.6's lane ladder', but its test cell is 'T110-2 (3), (5); T-V7-48'. Neither T110-2 clause lays a stage-2 seed: (3) runs S7's intervallum, and (5) runs a quay, an S5b road and an S5c street. The test that runs a stage-2 seed is V01's T-V1-51 (c) (V01 l. 3352), 'every ground crossing of a strip through an `open` span (a `vault` span under a wall read `open`, §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*) meeting §4.3's crossing rule', on its named `wallside` fixture. Round-6 note (6) (b) (i) asks each cell to name a test that runs it. The cell names V07's tracker test but not V01's seed test. Nothing built changes.

Row (a) of the way-and-channel table (base l. 2582) rules 'S7's quay, intervallum or castle path': each crosses the under-deck strip only by the crossing rule, and on failure ends 'at the strip as at a reservation'. §4.8's lead (l. 7692) restates this for 'a quay, the intervallum or a castle path', §4.3 (l. 5749) for 'S7's quays, intervallum and castle paths', and V11 row 80 lists the castle paths among `clearWidthM`'s readers. The row's test cell is 'T110-2 (3), (5)'. T110-2 (3) (l. 18562–18563) runs the intervallum, and (5) (l. 18586–18587) runs a quay. No clause in the set runs a castle path, meaning §4.8's internal paths (keep ↔ gatehouse ↔ wall stairs, l. 7762), crossing or ending at an under-deck strip; a search of the base and the volumes for 'castle path' or 'internal path' finds only the rule sites. The case is reachable on a common path. An aqueduct crosses a castle's bailey *over the band*, and S7 lays the internal paths after it: at generation where the S6 aqueduct crosses the bailey, and at every Regenerate (keep) of a document with a declared aqueduct there. A build that lays a castle path along the strip, or through a support ring, passes every bar. Under principle (11) and R6-01's grading, a defined edge that no bar runs is MAJOR.
issues.required_change: §13.2's T110-2 (3), after "… no ramp, stair or foot in the band or the channel, the stage's `N_k` gates on ground part 0;" (the clause's end, before "(4) *beneath* by hand"), add: "and a CITY fixture holding a declared masonry aqueduct across a corner of a castle's bailey (*over the band*), regenerated (keep), so that S7 lays the castle's internal paths (keep ↔ gatehouse ↔ wall stairs, §4.8) after it: each path crossing the under-deck strip under a span §4.3 admits or ending at the strip as at a reservation, 0 path corridors over a support ring, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span's strip (§2.7's way-and-channel table, row a);".

issues.claim: V01 §1.2's hook row (l. 205) reads '| V04 §3.5.4 (item 244's span rule) | a raised part's spans with their `use` (`open`, `vault`) | crossings through `open` spans only (V01 §3.17.3) |'. The span rule's home is the base's §2.7 (l. 2729, '**The span rule**, run eagerly at the end of the raised way's generation …'). V04 §3.5.4 (d) (V04 l. 1689–1690) is a reader of it: 'The base fixes each span's `use` eagerly by §2.7's span rule (item 244)'. This round makes the home matter more. A span's `use` is now read together with §2.7's crossing table (a `vault` span under a wall is read `open`; the span rule 'never reads a wall', l. 2644–2645), and V01 §3.17.3 (3) cites §2.7 for that reading, while the hook row still sends a builder to V04. The repair left the row as it stands, since it cites V01 §3.17.3 for its use; its provider column is the mis-citation. Nothing built changes.
issues.required_change: V01 §1.2's row: "V04 §3.5.4 (item 244's span rule)" → "§2.7's span rule (item 244; a `vault` span under a wall read `open`, §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*)", the other two cells as they stand.
